- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
ADAPY is a python library for structural analysis and design. It reads and
writes common CAD and FEM formats and can build, visualise and run analyses
on structural models.

Installing this package also provides the `ada` command-line tool. Run
`ada --help` for the full list of subcommands; these include `ada convert`
(convert between supported CAD/FEM formats), `ada view` (open a model in
the built-in web viewer) and `ada serve` (run the REST API or worker
process).

name: ada-py
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: ada-py
  version: "0.88.0"
  python_min: "3.11"

recipe:
  name: ${{ name }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/Krande/adapy/archive/v${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 2dd5ae1066208b5a94e3ff01e5e4013768e00879c3ef5eca3e8f667a81e3c84d

build:
  number: 0

outputs:
  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}-core
    build:
      noarch: python
      script: python -m pip install . --no-deps -vv
      python:
        entry_points:
          - ada=ada_cli.main:main
    requirements:
      host:
        - pip
        - setuptools
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
    about:
      description: |
        The core package without dependencies of ADAPY, a python library for structural analysis and design.

        This output ships the `ada` command-line entry point; most of its
        subcommands need the full `ada-py` package to be installed as well.

  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}
    build:
      noarch: python

    requirements:
      run:
        - python >=${{ python_min }}
        - numpy
        - hdf5
        - h5py
        - ifcopenshell
        - bcf-client
        # The CAD kernel. ada-cpp rather than pythonocc-core, because the geometry
        # layer's own path through it is the native one: ada.cad's backend registry
        # prefers ada-cpp when both are present, and the tessellation, STEP/IFC and
        # topology verbs it exposes are what adapy calls.
        #
        # This is also what lets the closure move to OCCT 8: pythonocc-core's newest
        # build is 7.9.3 and pins occt ==7.9.3, so requiring it holds every consumer
        # of ada-py on the 7.9 line regardless of what they themselves need.
        #
        # pythonocc-core is NOT gone, only un-required. `ada.occ` is unchanged and
        # ADAPY_CAD_BACKEND=occ still selects it; installing pythonocc-core alongside
        # is supported and is how anything reaching for an OCC capability ada-cpp does
        # not cover yet -- curved-face imprint is the live one -- keeps working.
        - ada-cpp
        - python-gmsh
        - pyquaternion
        # ada.api.animations / scene_converter build on trimesh's private glTF
        # internals (_data_append, the buffer_postprocessor bufferView
        # insertion-order contract), which the 5.0 major bump breaks. Upstream
        # locks/tests against 4.12.2; cap below 5 until adapy migrates.
        - trimesh >=5
        # No direct occt entry: it arrived with pythonocc-core and adapy links nothing
        # against it itself. ada-cpp carries the version it was built for, which is the
        # only one that can be right.
        - send2trash
        - meshio
        - websockets
        - plotly
        - python-kaleido
        - pydantic
        - ipywidgets
        - jupyterlab
        - pyparsing
        - pyglfw
        - pygfx
        - python-flatbuffers
        - openpyxl
        - ${{ pin_subpackage("ada-py-core", exact=True) }}
    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - ada
          pip_check: false
          python_version: ${{ python_min }}.*
      - files:
          source:
            - tests
            - files
        requirements:
          run:
            - python ${{ python_min }}.*
            - pytest
            - pytest-cov
            - pytest-asyncio
            - calculix
            - libgl-devel
            - mesalib
            - xorg-libxdamage
            - xorg-libxxf86vm
            - xorg-libxext
        script:
          # test_no_call_site_reimplements_the_env_parse greps the upstream src/ tree, which is not
          # part of the test files copied here; it is a repo lint, not a package test.
          # test_the_gate_can_actually_fail (assets layering gate AND clash vocabulary gate) uses
          # `git grep` to prove the forbidden tokens are findable -- the copied test-files tree
          # here has no .git of its own, so git grep searches the feedstock checkout around it and
          # silently finds nothing instead of erroring; a repo lint, not a package test. Both
          # gates read the installed package instead from the next adapy release, and these two
          # deselects can go then.
          # test_committed_frontend_fixture_is_current imports tools/gen_beam_solids_compact_fixture.py,
          # which lives outside the tests/ and files/ trees copied here.
          - pytest tests --ignore=tests/fem --ignore=tests/profiling --ignore=tests/examples --ignore=tests/full/frontend --ignore=tests/comms/rest --cov=ada --cov-report=xml --ignore=tests/core/visit/plotting/test_easy_plotly.py --deselect 
            tests/core/cad/test_tess_env_defaults.py::test_no_call_site_reimplements_the_env_parse --deselect tests/core/assets/test_layering_gate.py::test_the_gate_can_actually_fail --deselect tests/core/clash/test_vocabulary_gate.py::test_the_gate_can_actually_fail --deselect 
            tests/core/fem/results/test_beam_compact.py::test_committed_frontend_fixture_is_current

about:
  license: GPL-3.0-or-later
  license_file: LICENSE
  summary: A python library for structural analysis and design, plus the `ada` command-line tool
  description: |
    ADAPY is a python library for structural analysis and design. It reads and
    writes common CAD and FEM formats and can build, visualise and run analyses
    on structural models.

    Installing this package also provides the `ada` command-line tool. Run
    `ada --help` for the full list of subcommands; these include `ada convert`
    (convert between supported CAD/FEM formats), `ada view` (open a model in
    the built-in web viewer) and `ada serve` (run the REST API or worker
    process).
  homepage: https://github.com/krande/adapy
  documentation: https://krande.github.io/adapy/

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - Krande
